## Proof

**Claim:** Yes, for any permutation $\sigma \in S_n$, the element $g_1 g_2 \cdots g_n\, g_{\sigma(1)}^{-1} g_{\sigma(2)}^{-1} \cdots g_{\sigma(n)}^{-1}$ lies in the commutator subgroup $G'$.

**Proof.**

Let $w = g_1 g_2 \cdots g_n\, g_{\sigma(1)}^{-1} g_{\sigma(2)}^{-1} \cdots g_{\sigma(n)}^{-1}$.

Recall that $G' = [G,G]$ is the commutator subgroup, and the quotient $G/G'$ (the abelianization) is the largest abelian quotient of $G$. An element $x \in G$ belongs to $G'$ if and only if its image $\bar{x}$ in $G/G'$ is the identity.

Consider the image of $w$ in $G/G'$. Denote the image of $g_i$ by $\bar{g}_i$. Since $G/G'$ is abelian, the order of multiplication does not matter, so:

$$\bar{w} = \bar{g}_1 \bar{g}_2 \cdots \bar{g}_n \cdot \bar{g}_{\sigma(1)}^{-1} \bar{g}_{\sigma(2)}^{-1} \cdots \bar{g}_{\sigma(n)}^{-1} = \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n} \bar{g}_i\right) \cdot \left(\prod_{j=1}^{n} \bar{g}_{\sigma(j)}^{-1}\right).$$

Since $\sigma$ is a permutation of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$, the multiset $\{g_{\sigma(1)}, g_{\sigma(2)}, \ldots, g_{\sigma(n)}\}$ is exactly $\{g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_n\}$. Therefore, in the abelian group $G/G'$:

$$\prod_{j=1}^{n} \bar{g}_{\sigma(j)} = \prod_{i=1}^{n} \bar{g}_i,$$

and consequently

$$\prod_{j=1}^{n} \bar{g}_{\sigma(j)}^{-1} = \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n} \bar{g}_i\right)^{-1}.$$

Substituting back:

$$\bar{w} = \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n} \bar{g}_i\right) \cdot \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n} \bar{g}_i\right)^{-1} = 1.$$

Since $\bar{w} = 1$ in $G/G'$, we conclude $w \in G'$. $\blacksquare$
